qa.q: Which part of your country do most people live in?
qa.a: Well most people live in cities and other population centers and what's called the central belt so that's close to the border with England. Actually it's north of the border with England but it's located deeper into the country than the highlands and islands. All of the major cities are near the coast although I think that's a common trait in just about every country to be honest, every country with a coastline.

qa.q: What are the main industries in your country?
qa.a: Well until recently the hospitality industry was probably our mainstay along with tourism. Everybody wants to see the highlands and islands and take pictures next to people wearing kilts. I think we have some significant exports in terms of food and beverages as well like everybody has heard of whiskey in haggis and Scottish fudge for example so it's quite there those are the main ones but you can see they're quite varied.

qa.q: What are some of the good things about living in your country?
qa.a: Well for all the jokes that we tell about like freedom we have a lot of freedom and wealth. For all the people complain that we don't I think our country is actually quite prosperous. It's not perfect and it's not prosperous and great all the time but we do a pretty good job of striking a good balance between constraining and encouraging people. It could always be improved but I think there are a few other places that do a better job than how we do it.

qa.q: What are some of the bad things about living in your country?
qa.a: Well I suppose one of the downsides of people having so much opportunity is that they do things that aren't always beneficial for society. We have problems with people having terrible health conditions for example mentally and physically. A lot of the time though these detrimental sides to things come about as a result of poor personal choices so in the same way they can be fixed by people making the right ones which they've got the opportunity to make.
